(1) the finite strength of the lithosphere has a major impact on the development of sedimentary basins; (2) the strength of the lithospheric extensional and compressional regimes can be quantified by means of finite element models; (3) quantitative sedimentary basin models are capable of incorporating the effects of finite lithospheric strength; and (4) the integration of surface processes and lithospheric deformation in sedimentary basin models is feasible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of integrated models that link the lithosphere with the basin fill, and the development of a quantitative framework for the analysis of the sedimentary record.
the quantitative investigation of the interaction between surface and lithospheric processes.
the development of integrated models that couple surface processes with lithospheric processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the integration of different models for lithospherical and surface processes is a necessary prerequisite for the successful quantitative modeling of the sedimentary record.

the mechanical properties of the lithospheric plate and surface processes, including sediment supply, erosion and tectonic deformation, must be incorporated in a fully integrated manner into the modeling of sedimentary basins.
the integration of lithospheric and basin fill modeling provides a powerful tool to investigate the interplay of surface processes with lithospheric deformation in compressional settings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the integration of different surface and subsurface processes, such as lithospheric flexural deformation and surface processes, in quantitative stratigraphic modeling is now possible and has been demonstrated to be effective.

quantitative modeling of sedimentary basins has now reached a level of sophistication to allow for a more integrated treatment of the mechanical and surface processes that govern sedimentary basin evolution.

the coupling of surface processes to the mechanical evolution of the lithosphere has led to a better understanding of the interplay between the lithospheric strength and the stratigraphic evolution of sedimentary basins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of lithospheric and basin modeling is a prerequisite for the development of quantitative models for basin stratigraphy.
the mechanical properties of the lithospheric plate are critical in determining the geometry of the basin fill and the timing and distribution of synsedimentary deformation.
the integration of lithospheric and sedimentary processes in basin models is a powerful means to address fundamental questions on the interplay between surface and lithospheric processes.
